analysis:
Examined both files' metadata, the complete composite action before/after, and every supplied workflow hunk. The changes concern CI source/dependency/build-cache custody, relevant to artifact integrity (A-011, A-017, T-013, T-054), not runtime prompt caching (T-041). No supplied change modifies authorization, attestation, encryption, billing, inference cancellation, or local privileged interfaces.
.github/actions/provider-ci-build/action.yml:7-9,107,116,143 defaults cache writes off and requires explicit caller opt-in. ci.yml:19 limits that opt-in to master/dev push events and passes it to each shown build lane. This narrows previous write conditions. The new SwiftPM repository cache (action.yml:47-53,115-120) partitions by OS, workspace/home layout, lane and lockfiles, with broader fallback within the lane; no adversarial writer into trusted branch scope is established.
ci.yml:57-101 introduces daily .git caching before checks execute, disables checkout credential persistence, and retries cold after checkout failure. The repeated checkout blocks preserve recursive submodules where previously requested; Docs Lint uses a separate full-history cache family and blob filtering (171-211). Sparse checkout excludes evidence archives/videos elsewhere. The cluster key retains submodule commit/path identity while removing describe text (962). No concrete security regression is supported by these changes alone.
Integration should reconcile retained Git refs and partial-clone behavior with frozen-source provenance checks invoked after Docs Lint checkout (base 118 onward/head 194 onward), and confirm sparse exclusions do not remove inputs required by release-integrity checks. Those check implementations and complete workflow surroundings are outside this supplied scope; their compatibility is an unresolved contract, not evidence of bypass. Actual artifact signing/qualification remains outside this local review.
